evidence.paraphrase: The paper tests whether a structural marginal-cost Phillips curve can explain U.S. inflation persistence better than an output-gap specification.

evidence.locator_label: Calvo pricing and hybrid Phillips curve
evidence.paraphrase: Inflation depends on expected future inflation and real marginal cost; a hybrid extension adds lagged inflation when some firms use backward-looking pricing rules.
Rational-expectations forecast errors generate moment conditions with lagged information; GMM estimates structural coefficients and maps them into price-duration parameters.
Forward and hybrid models, output-gap versus labor-share proxies, instrument sets, subsamples, and overidentification results are compared before interpreting inflation inertia.

executive_summary: Galí and Gertler derive a New Keynesian Phillips curve from Calvo pricing, replace the conventional output gap with real marginal cost proxied by labor income share, and estimate both forward-looking and hybrid specifications by GMM. The paper makes instruments, orthogonality conditions, price-stickiness mapping, and overidentification central to interpretation; it is a template for structural inflation estimation, not a generic OLS Phillips curve.
